5308.title: Build and validate generated samples in isolated test workspaces
5308.body:
Build and validate generated samples in isolated test workspaces (#5308)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5291
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1630344

Validate the package-consuming applications distributed in sample archives
through an ordinary .NET test suite. Keep repository build settings out of
consumer workspaces, retain evidence after cleanup, and exercise real sample
builds and host/container execution rather than synthetic substitutes.

Carry forward the sample foundation from #5291 without replacing the existing
Integration or MSBuild suites, package-output cases, device tests, or goldens.
This change does not alter shipped managed APIs or the native ABI.

~~ Make generated sample validation discoverable ~~

Replace samples.cake's imperative solution and Docker run.ps1 loops with the
net10.0 SkiaSharp.Tests.Samples runner. Remove samples-prepare and samples-run;
samples now generates the inputs and invokes the test project. Direct
dotnet test and IDE execution consume those prepared inputs without invoking
Cake or acquiring packages.

SampleLookup selects host-specific SLNX variants and Dockerfiles. Basic and
Gallery theories build the eligible generated solutions with their declared
TFMs unchanged; Gallery, WASM, and Blazor coverage is build-only. Discovery
tests assert the expected host case sets independently of build execution
and Docker availability.

Include SkiaSharp and the runner's macOS/Win32 native-assets dependencies in
the Samples solution. Document net10.0 global properties for solution runs so
those dependency projects do not build their entire shipping TFM matrix.

Keep the existing three CI host jobs, acquire native artifacts for the
repository-based runner alongside the consumer NuGet packages, and publish
TRX results and diagnostic artifacts even when tests fail. Samples disable
MTP's activity-based hang monitor because it misdetects child build process
trees; the child commands retain their own bounded lifetimes.

Build 1630344 passed its stages at source 7ea57f453ff2, tested through merge
23e50175f022: Windows 112 passed, Linux 105 passed, and macOS 107 passed with
four Docker-availability skips. Linux's first attempt failed before tests on
a truncated Emscripten archive; the authorized Linux-only retry preserved
the successful Windows/macOS attempts. This full result predates the later
shared-runner changes and is not exact-head proof for 2180818e7cb.

~~ Require generated dependencies to match the producing packages ~~

Generated samples must restore the supplied product packages rather than
silently selecting public releases or a different producing build. Preserve
explicit generation versions from VERSIONS.txt and the supplied suffix.
Before runner restore/build, require one non-symbol core package for each
of SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp and matching producing suffixes. Generated
project contracts check that declared product versions exist in the cohort.

Native-assets project references need their concrete project name as the
package ID, not the broader PackagingGroup used to obtain the family version.
Add Linux.NoDependencies references to Console and Web: their generated Linux
runtime checks previously failed before rendering because libSkiaSharp.so
was absent.

Expose Views, Skottie, and Linux native dependencies before the source-only
Uno import in Basic and Gallery. The in-tree helper replaces earlier project
references with platform-selected references; generation instead converts
the declarations into versioned packages. Keep Gallery Shared after that
import so the helper does not remove it. Stamp SkiaSharpVersion in Basic Uno,
Gallery Uno, and SkiaFiddle to align Uno's implicit product references.

Package-contract tests exercise missing, duplicate, and mismatched core
inputs, explicit generated dependencies, and Uno version overrides. Basic
and Gallery Uno desktop/browser source builds also passed, preserving the
in-tree path alongside the generated consumer path.

~~ Separate consumer SDK and cache state from the repository runner ~~

A consumer build below the repository would otherwise inherit global.json,
Directory.Build imports, and ambient restore/build environment variables.
Prepare a per-test workspace containing the selected sample, required
ancestor configuration, and Gallery's shared sibling projects rather than
copying unrelated samples.

Place empty Directory.Build fences and a host-selecting SDK section at the
workspace root, not around the repository test runner. Reject sample-local
global.json files that would override that boundary. Preserve the host PATH
while clearing inherited DOTNET, MSBuild, restore, and NuGet settings; place
CLI home and package/HTTP/scratch caches inside the disposable workspace.

Map SkiaSharp* and HarfBuzzSharp* restores to the supplied artifact source,
with public feeds available for other dependencies. Remove the old
samples-prepare package-cache clearing: consumer isolation must not require
deleting another build's cached packages.

Infrastructure tests verify scoped copying, ancestor configuration, SDK
selection despite a deliberately invalid repository pin, private cache
paths, artifact-source mappings, and preservation of neighboring workspaces.

~~ Bound owned-directory cleanup without hiding permanent failures ~~

Terminated Windows descendants can briefly retain DLL handles. Retry owned
directory deletion for sharing, lock, and access-denied error codes, bounded
to 20 attempts with 250 ms waits; unrelated errors and exhausted retries
remain failures.

macOS recursive deletion can encounter ENOTEMPTY after metadata appears in
an enumerated directory. Permit one immediate, logged retry for HResult 66
when the remaining tree contains directories and .DS_Store files. Reject
symlinks, unrelated residue, other errors, and persistent writers rather
than treating deletion failure as successful cleanup.

Regression tests exercise metadata-only recovery, unrelated errors and
files, persistent writers, Windows handle release, and preservation of
diagnostics and neighboring resources. Diagnostics live outside disposable
consumer roots.

~~ Exercise real applications while owning their process and Docker lifetime ~~

Run the host Console/Web applications and the existing Docker Console/Web
samples through shared application callbacks. Check Console exit codes and
output, HTTP status/content types, readiness endpoints, and rendered PNGs.
Host HTTP binds to an ephemeral loopback port; request construction rejects
origin changes, fragments, and malformed paths.

Bound tool and application execution, terminate owned process trees, and
retain separate stdout/stderr plus available build binlogs. Attach files up
to 8 MiB to test results; larger diagnostics remain in pipeline artifacts.

Docker fixtures use unique tags, contexts, and container names, reuse their
own built images, and remove their own resources. Replace the old global
docker system prune --all --force cleanup; aggregate owned cleanup failures
instead of silently swallowing them. Keep the existing .NET 10 Dockerfiles.

Probe Docker availability with a bounded docker info request. Missing CLI,
an unavailable daemon, or a probe timeout produces a visible skip; incorrect
container mode and actual build/runtime failures remain failures. Apply
availability checks on macOS too, rather than excluding the platform, while
leaving macOS CI daemon provisioning absent.

Local macOS validation passed 94 checks with usable Docker. Missing-daemon
and missing-CLI runs each passed 90 checks and visibly skipped four Docker
cases, demonstrating availability behavior without changing shared resources.

~~ Render container text without relying on installed system fonts ~~

Minimal containers did not provide a usable default typeface, leaving the
sample text absent despite successful image creation. Bundle the existing
Noto Sans font with Docker Console and Docker WebApi, copy it to build and
publish output, and load it explicitly through SKTypeface.FromFile.

Retain font attribution and the SIL Open Font License link in the sample
READMEs, including the Android/Blazor samples already using Noto Sans.
Real container executions and reviewed before/after images establish the
rendering correction rather than a font-load-only assertion.

~~ Compare decoded sample pixels with a narrowly bounded allowance ~~

Add reviewed host and container PNG references under the Samples suite.
Compare decoded pixels rather than encoded file bytes, require matching
dimensions, and retain zero per-channel tolerance. Permit at most 0.075% of
pixels to differ, using decimal arithmetic so fractional thresholds do not
round upward.

Keep this policy local to sample output; core image comparisons and GPU
policies are unchanged. Missing references fail, mismatches retain actual
and difference images, and tests do not accept replacement goldens.

Boundary tests accept 360 changed pixels at 800x600 but reject 361, and
accept 196 at 512x512 but reject 197. Fractional-size cases and one-level
color/alpha changes verify that the allowance counts differing pixels,
not a relaxed channel threshold.

~~ Expose live test progress while preserving caller configuration ~~

Long CI runs appeared stalled at InvokeTestingPlatform because MTP captured
runner output. Default TestingPlatformCaptureOutput to false in the cloned
RunDotNetTest property dictionary and pass --show-live-output on --no-ansi.
Keep the device runner unchanged and do not force the SDK terminal logger
off or claim that buffered child-build output now streams line by line.

Use TryAdd for Platform and optional coverage properties, emitting each
quoted property through the shared loop. Preserve explicit caller values
and the caller's original dictionary. Allow the Samples caller to build the
runner and opt out of activity-based hang detection while retaining the
default TRX and 15-minute Mini hang-dump behavior for other callers.

Actual Cake helper probes passed with default capture=false and explicit
capture=true, confirming live default heartbeats and retained TRX/hang
arguments. Further probes passed for coverage defaults, explicit overrides
including a spaced output path, and coverage disabled. These checks prove
argument handling, not coverage instrumentation or another full-suite run.

~~ Write exported quick starts for generated-copy consumers ~~

Use sample-local run/publish commands and concise application guidance in
Gallery, MAUI, Uno, and SkiaFiddle READMEs. Remove repository implementation
inventories and source-checkout bootstrap instructions from these exported
consumer entry points; generation removes repository-native imports and
converts product references to packages.

Keep repository setup, explicit producing-version arguments, IDE/direct
test commands, and failure diagnostics in building-samples.md and central
maintainer guidance. Bootstrap must precede staging packages because it
resets output; native changes require source builds rather than downloaded
binaries.

Review raised the omitted in-tree bootstrap in four quick starts. The
maintainer confirmed their generated-consumer audience, so those findings
were resolved without adding repository setup to package-based instructions.
Also remove obsolete cross-sample links and repository-location claims from
the portable README/media guidance.

5317.title: Preserve canonical producer build identity across midnight
5317.body:
Preserve canonical pipeline build identity across later jobs (#5317)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5266
Context: 1934d9ee3a7ed014d4825c8b7b9e954f54513513
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1629289
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1630000

Keep package producers and later consumers on the identity established by
Prepare, and place that pipeline-wide responsibility in shared infrastructure.

~~ Preserve producer identity instead of recomputing it per job ~~

Build 1629289 packaged with OfficialBuildId 20261008.29 and build number
26508.29, but its later MacSamples job computed 20261009.2 and 26509.2.
The run already had the producer's canonical product name; the script ignored
that name unless it came from a downstream pipeline resource.

Reuse BUILD_BUILDNUMBER when it contains the current product version.
Parse its prerelease label and build number, or its stable official ID, and
restore ARCADE_OFFICIAL_BUILD_ID from the dated identity for signing metadata.
Retain resource-run precedence for Manual and ResourceTrigger consumers.
Resource consumers still inherit BUILD_COUNTER; same-run jobs leave their
separate transport counter untouched. Legacy undated identities do not invent
an official ID, and malformed product names fail instead of silently drifting.

Regression fixtures exercise different later-job dates and revisions, PR and
release identities, resource precedence, year boundaries, and invocation
without updating the run name. The new midnight regression failed against the
base script and passed with the fix.

Azure build 1630000 passed its native, managed, packaging, test, MSBuild and
sample stages for head ac0b81e8d2ab365377f9bde88770a786592ca3fc. Its 92 executed
identity steps retained build number 26509.8 and transport counter 2806.
An audit of the produced nuspecs found no version discrepancies: 55 product
packages used 4.156.0-pr.5317.26509.8 or 14.4.0.100-pr.5317.26509.8, and
23 transport packages used 0.0.0-pr.5317.2806. Their 327 dependencies on
produced packages matched those versions; product repository commits matched
the tested head. Transport templates continue omitting repository metadata.

This public run does not exercise internal signing. The separate Windows
source benchmark in Actions run 37956224275 failed because MSVC 14.44.35207
lacked matching x64 Spectre libraries, so the complete PR check set is not
green. That toolchain provisioning is unchanged by this identity fix.

~~ Put pipeline-wide identity scripts in shared infrastructure ~~

Move set-build-variables.ps1 and its behavioral tests from
scripts/infra/native/shared/ to scripts/infra/shared/. The native directory
implied a narrower responsibility than the existing callers: Prepare, managed
and native jobs, packaging, samples, coverage, and signing share the script.

Update the pipeline callers and documentation references, and adjust the
test's repository-root calculation for its shallower location. The relocation
does not change script contents. The relocated tests passed locally and in
Prepare; cache coverage validation reported no uncovered tracked files.

5306.title: Align .NET 11 preview pins and WASM native assets
5306.body:
Align .NET 11 preview pins and WASM native assets (#5306)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5291
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1628616

Keep the preview SDK, native archive builds and consumer target selection
aligned without changing stable framework mappings or replacing the existing
SDK provisioning and MSBuild test infrastructure. Carry forward the SDK/WASM
work from #5291 as an independently mergeable change.

~~ Provision the preview toolchain from approved feeds ~~

Approved mirrors lacked Preview 6's Emscripten 5.0.6 host packs. Advance the
preview lane to SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 and workload set
11.0.100-rc.1.26460.1 without adding feeds. Leave stable and WinUI SDK pins,
Tizen's existing variable/interface, and declared project frameworks unchanged.

Replace the four Emscripten 5.0.6 native build variants with 6.0.2, retaining
single-threaded, multithreaded, SIMD and SIMD+threading combinations and their
_wasmeh/_newexc flags. Replace their artifact names in both the aggregate
native merger and the WASM-specific merger so package production consumes the
new toolchain. Do not retain obsolete preview-only 5.0.6 production jobs.

Build 1628616 tested PR merge d261c6e837f5f829ea2cc3781f86d7dac287cdfc,
which includes head 7acc32856576ca4f8272596246450d03bcf61447. Its four 6.0.2
native jobs, WASM artifact merger, and stable and preview WASM test jobs passed.
These job results do not establish success of the entire multi-platform build.

~~ Select matching archives across the .NET 11 boundary ~~

The source targets and packaged HarfBuzz targets selected 5.0.6 for net11+,
while packaged Skia still selected 3.1.56 for every framework at or above
net9. Updating the compiler alone would leave consumers selecting archives
from the wrong toolchain.

Align the source and buildTransitive targets for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp:
net8 selects 3.1.34, net9/net10 select 3.1.56, and net11+ selects 6.0.2. Cap
packaged Skia's 3.1.56 predicate below 11.0 and add its missing net11+ entry.
Keep the newest predicate open-ended; the mapping applies to .NET 11 targets,
not a separate RC1-only target category. Update package and upgrade guidance
to describe the same framework boundaries.

~~ Verify evaluated native references without claiming linkage ~~

The existing package-output tests inspect desktop native binaries, not WASM
static archive selection. Add WasmTargetsSelectTheDeclaredFrameworkToolchain
to that existing MSBuild host rather than importing the Samples runner.

Copy the four repository targets into per-test workspaces and evaluate
NativeFileReference with real MSBuild. Five framework rows, net8 through
net12, exercise both families, source/package imports, and threading/SIMD
combinations: 80 evaluations assert one item and its exact FullPath. Include
an obsolete 5.0.6 fixture to detect accidental old-toolchain selection.

Pass the repository directory through runtime configuration and share the
existing command execution, environment filtering and diagnostic capture.
Evaluation has a one-minute timeout; build/publish retain five minutes.
Preserve the existing 48 package-output cases and their MSBuild CI stage.

The five regression rows passed locally with SDK 10.0.401 and the pinned
SDK 11, with no skipped cases. Dummy archives prove item selection only;
they cannot prove native linking or execution. Those require producing CI
and the WASM runtime tests, rather than old downloaded native binaries.

5307.title: Simplify SDK and workload provisioning with explicit descriptors
5307.body:
Simplify SDK and workload provisioning with explicit descriptors (#5307)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5291

Separate SDK acquisition, workload installation and build SDK selection.
Make job requirements declarative while retaining standard UseDotNet@2
acquisition, existing build/test orchestration and repository version pins.

~~ Make host provisioning requirements explicit ~~

The bootstrapper combined install switches, additional SDKs, workload
strings and preview-specific setup. Replace that interface with dotnetSdks
descriptors containing sdkVersion, optional workloadSetVersion, optional
workload IDs and optional Samsung manifest metadata.

The generic default now installs the repository SDK without workloads.
Omitting workloadSetVersion makes an entry SDK-only; an empty dotnetSdks
list opts out of host provisioning. Managed, package, core/device test and
existing Samples jobs explicitly retain their workload requirements.
Container and merger callers explicitly opt out rather than depending on
job-name or Docker conditions inside the SDK installer.

Keep the existing host workload lists, including Linux's android, macos,
wasm-tools and maui-android requirements and the managed jobs' Tizen setup.
Preserve the Android-only override. WinUI/ANGLE entries are SDK-only, and
WinUI's side-by-side SDK declaration replaces its redundant prebuild
UseDotNet tasks. Retain the Samples and MSBuild stages, Cake entry points,
180-minute job limit, cache-skip conditions and three-retry task policy.

Remove the unused install-dotnet.ps1 custom downloader/PATH setup and
install-maui.ps1 global maui-check --fix flow. SDK acquisition remains with
UseDotNet@2; requested workloads go through install-dotnet-workloads.ps1.
Document the descriptor contract and its separate selection rules.

Keep the website side build independent of this provisioning contract. Its
existing setup-dotnet/global.json acquisition and standalone, unpinned
'dotnet workload install wasm-tools' command remain unchanged.

Parsed 53 Azure/GitHub YAML files and checked the supported interface on
47 bootstrapper callers. The existing cache coverage audit reports no
uncovered tracked files, including the new shared steps template.

~~ Select the SDK explicitly without replacing repository configuration ~~

Installing an SDK does not select it. WinUI demonstrates why selecting the
last installed SDK would be wrong: repository tooling uses 10.0.401 while
native/winui/global.json selects its side-by-side 10.0.111 SDK.

Ordinary jobs keep their global.json selection. Preview WASM and MSBuild
package-test jobs use jobSdkVersion explicitly. Unlike the old preview
step, which replaced global.json with an SDK-only object, activation edits
its SDK fields, disables roll-forward and verifies dotnet --version while
preserving tools and MSBuild configuration. It does not repin Arcade's
tools.dotnet acquisition setting.

Workload installation also receives an exact SDK instead of inheriting the
repository's current selection. Run it from a GUID-owned temporary
context with an exact-sdk global.json, disabled roll-forward and a version
check. Restore the working directory and remove that context in finally
blocks; installed workloads remain available to subsequent job steps.
Missing SDKs and nonzero workload-install exits fail explicitly.

Install the Microsoft workload IDs once with --version and the repository
nuget.config. Keep SDK 10.0.401 and workload set 10.0.202 separate: the
existing cross-feature-band pin avoids the newer set's Xcode requirement.
The existing preview SDK/workload pins are unchanged. Do not add a root
global.json workloadVersion that SDK-only native jobs would also consume.

PowerShell syntax and exact job activation checks passed, including
preservation of non-SDK configuration and missing-SDK failure cleanup.
A fresh 10.0.401 SDK installed wasm-tools with set 10.0.202 without changing
repository global.json. The unfiltered net10.0 console solution was not
green: 6,396 tests passed, 47 declared skips remained and the known
macOS-arm64 ganesh-gl/DiagonalLines golden mismatch still failed. No golden
or skip-policy changes are included.

~~ Register Samsung manifests beside the executable actually being used ~~

Tizen is not part of Microsoft's workload set. Separate Samsung's
publication band 10.0.100 from manifest version 10.0.123 and from the
consuming SDK's feature band. Require both Samsung pins when Tizen is
requested; the helper also requires at least one Microsoft workload ID.

Download the pinned manifest from dotnet-public and register it under both
the publication and consuming SDK bands, preserving preview/RC band
suffixes. Replace the old Get-Command/readlink path handling with the first
PATH application and .NET symlink resolution. Select-Object -First 1 is
necessary because Get-Command -CommandType Application can return several
matches. An inherited DOTNET_ROOT is not authority for that destination.
Log the resolved installation root to expose misplaced-manifest failures.

Install Tizen separately after the pinned Microsoft workloads, using the
same repository feeds and --skip-manifest-update so it does not refresh
the Microsoft manifests. Keep downloaded/extracted temporary files inside
the helper-owned context instead of the former shared output/tmp paths.

The real provisioning exercise covered a symlink, multiple PATH matches
and a deliberately divergent DOTNET_ROOT. Tizen 10.0.123 was registered in
the selected SDK's 10.0.400 band and installed alongside wasm-tools; the
inherited root and repository global.json remained unchanged.

5302.title: Fix GTK4 test hosting and internal CI build failures
5302.body:
Fix GTK4 test hosting and internal CI build failures (#5302)

Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1623952
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3097813
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3098649
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1627426
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3098733
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3098935
Context: https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/section-threading.html
Context: https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.GLArea.get_allowed_apis.html

Align CI tests with provisioned GTK runtimes and approved package feeds, and
bound native-input downloads without weakening their verification. Change
CI/test setup rather than production views, GPU skip policy or rendering
goldens.

Public 1627426 passed PR merge e5948f38; internal packaging 3098733 and
connected Tests 3098935 passed head c45a0a60e63, with Tests consuming package
build 3098733.

~~ Keep the MAUI gallery on approved feeds ~~

Internal 3097813 failed Secure Supply Chain Analysis with CFS0013 because the
gallery's nuget.config added nuget.org. Remove that source, retain <clear/>,
dotnet-public and dotnet-eng, and keep the policy enabled. A fresh-cache
net10.0-maccatalyst restore passed using those feeds; internal packaging
subsequently passed the policy gate.

~~ Run GTK4-native tests on provisioned hosts ~~

EpoxyExportsGlDispatchPointers still attempted to load libepoxy when widget
tests were skipped. Public 1623952's macOS run failed with DllNotFoundException
for libepoxy.0.dylib. Gate SkiaSharp.Views.Gtk4.Tests on IsRunningOnLinux() in
the desktop .NET Core recipe, using existing GTK4/Xvfb provisioning rather than
adding a GTK4/libepoxy installation to Windows and macOS jobs.

Keep the core, singleton-init, Vulkan and Direct3D hosts unconditional. Public
1627426's Windows and macOS .NET Core suites passed with this split.

~~ Serialize GTK4 test collections ~~

SKDrawingAreaTest and SKGLAreaTest initialize and access the shared GTK runtime,
but xUnit could execute their collections concurrently. Disable collection
parallelism for the GTK4 assembly because GTK widget operations are not
thread-safe. This prevents overlapping collections; it does not implement GTK
main-thread dispatch. The assembly's 32 tests passed in public 1627426.

~~ Assert GLArea state with GTK 4.6-compatible APIs ~~

InitialStateDoesNotRequireGlContext called gtk_gl_area_get_allowed_apis, which
was introduced in GTK 4.12 and is absent from Ubuntu 22.04's GTK 4.6. Drop the
allowed-APIs assertion and check auto-render is false and stencil buffering is
true, matching setters already present in the SKGLArea constructor. Verify
constructor state without requiring a GL context. The existing suite passed on
GTK 4.6.9; the initial-state case also passed in public 1627426.

~~ Retry interrupted fontconfig downloads and fail explicitly ~~

The Linux x64 job in 3098649 lost the pinned libfontconfig1 2.12.6-0ubuntu2
amd64 transfer with curl (56), then hashed a nonexistent file and reported a
misleading empty-hash mismatch. Missing-output and SBOM errors were downstream
of that failed transfer.

Update the fontconfig loops in glibc and glibc-x86 to use --retry 3
--retry-all-errors, a 30-second connection timeout and a 300-second transfer
limit per attempt. Append || exit 1 to curl: bash -e did not stop the old loop
inside its surrounding && chain. Preserve package versions, SHA-256 pins and
checksum-before-extraction guards.

Fault injection verified reset/partial-response recovery and exhaustion after
four attempts before checksum or extraction. The interrupted amd64 package was
separately downloaded and matched its existing pin; the internal Linux x64
native job subsequently passed.

5250.title: Add XAML-based MAUI gallery and consistent live filters
5250.body:
Add XAML-based MAUI gallery and consistent live filters (#5250)

Context: https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/33800
Context: https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/33818
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3178

Add a native MAUI gallery host alongside Blazor and Uno, sharing the
same sample catalog, built from XAML pages and controls with typed
compiled bindings instead of a code-constructed visual tree. Extend the
animated-sample lifecycle safety and the live, alphabetical,
empty-hiding facet behavior this required to every gallery host, and
fix a Mac Catalyst finalizer crash surfaced by the dependency the new
host needed.

~~ Add a native, XAML-first MAUI gallery host ~~

Blazor and Uno already shared one sample catalog; hand-constructing
Microsoft.Maui.Controls visual trees in C# for a third host would have
abandoned MAUI's own XAML/binding model. Rewrite every gallery page,
control, template, and popover as XAML with typed x:DataType compiled
bindings, keeping C# only for navigation, native rendering lifetime,
and collection replacement. The host adds shared app chrome, a
responsive sidebar-or-popover filter rail, per-window CPU/GPU and
System/Light/Dark theme selection, a controls panel that collapses to
an overlay button on the canvas in wide layouts, native document export
through Launcher/Share, and a Debug-only DevFlow agent.

  * Compiled bindings resolve x:DataType members by reflection against
    the binding context's public surface; marking a presentation-model
    property or collection internal fails silently at runtime (no
    compile error, an empty or unbound control) despite a clean build.
    Make every presentation type (CategoryFacet, TagFacet, ActiveFacet,
    MenuOptionItem, SampleTagItem, GalleryCardItem, ControlItem, and
    each page's list properties) public, and enable
    MauiStrictXamlCompilation and
    MauiEnableXamlCBindingWithSourceCompilation to catch this class of
    mistake at compile time.
  * A live, attached CollectionView cannot have its
    GridItemsLayout.Span mutated during a window-resize callback on Mac
    Catalyst/.NET 10: UICollectionView.setCollectionViewLayout(animated)
    hangs inside the resize transition. The host instead replaces the
    whole CollectionView, preconfigured with the new span and detached
    from its old handler, at each column-count breakpoint.
  * AutomationId is immutable once set, and CollectionView recycles
    cell views, so a recycled cell cannot be renumbered for a different
    sample. Give each distinct bound sample a freshly constructed card,
    compared by reference, so only genuinely new content gets a new
    AutomationId.
  * Resetting Picker.SelectedIndex from inside its own
    SelectedIndexChanged handler reenters MAUI's internal
    SelectedItem/SelectedIndex sync and hangs, so tag selection ignores
    a duplicate add rather than clearing SelectedIndex.
  * Slider.Minimum/Maximum setters can recoerce Value and refire
    ValueChanged while MAUI is still applying the initial binding,
    before the real model value is set, silently corrupting defaults
    (Nine-Patch width reset to 100 instead of 400). Use TwoWay
    bindings, guard the view's change handlers with an applyingContext
    flag during OnBindingContextChanged, and call
    ControlItem.Refresh() afterward to restore the canonical value.

A new scripts/smoke.py drives a running Debug build through one
persistent MAUI DevFlow batch session and renders/navigates 32 of the
catalog's 33 samples that support a live preview (Create XPS Document
has no document preview on this platform) on both CPU and Metal, plus
search, popovers, theme, sort, resize, controls-collapse, slider/picker
stepping, and PDF export. The new SkiaSharp.Gallery.Tests.Console
project adds 50 passing regression tests, Mac Catalyst Debug and
Release both build with zero XamlC warnings, and the unfiltered core
suite passes 6339 tests with 23 declared skips and one pre-existing,
unrelated golden-image mismatch (ganesh-gl/DiagonalLines).

~~ Serialize animated samples against cancellation and disposal ~~

Lottie, GIF, animated-WebP-encoder, and shader playground/cross-fade
samples ran their own timer-driven animation loop independently of the
hosting page's lifecycle; a loop iteration could still mutate native
Skia state after the page called Destroy(), and a background sample
instance's pending async work could bleed into a newer visit of the
same sample.

Give SampleBase/CanvasSampleBase a SyncRoot, a captured cancellation
token per animation loop (delay outside the lock, mutate and recheck
the token inside it), and an AnimationFailed event instead of
swallowing a failed frame silently. SampleService.CreateSample now
returns an independent instance per visit so an old instance can never
touch a new one's state, and SampleDetailPage locks the same SyncRoot
around Paint, ChangeControl, and GenerateDocument so UI-thread control
updates cannot race the render loop either. Any future animated sample
must follow the same "delay outside the lock, mutate and check the
token inside the lock" pattern. The new gallery regression suite covers
these lifecycle races, and the full smoke pass exercises playback,
pause/resume, and renderer switching on every animated sample.

~~ Make every gallery's facets live, alphabetical, and uncluttered ~~

Typing in the search box left disabled categories and tags showing
their full-corpus counts instead of the current match count, so a
filter combination with zero results still listed every category as
selectable. Tag order differed per host. Uno's category chips were a
multi-select HashSet with a confusing Clear/All toggle, while Blazor
and MAUI already used a single selected category. Blazor's empty-state
copy also told users to "switch tag mode to ANY," a mode never wired to
anything: tagModeAll is a private field hardcoded to true.

Add SampleManager.OrderTags() (alphabetical by displayed name, full-
identity tiebreak) and GetCategoryCounts() (computed from the currently
filtered results, not the full catalog). Blazor's FilterRail,
SampleCard, and ActiveFilterBar, the Uno HomePage category chips, and
the MAUI rail and detail tag strips all sort through OrderTags() and
hide zero-count facets while still letting an active filter be
removed. Uno's selectedCategories HashSet becomes a single
selectedCategory to match Blazor and MAUI, each visible chip shows its
live count, and a result set of zero surfaces a "Reset filters" action
instead of leaving every chip visibly matching nothing. Remove the
stale "ANY" empty-state copy. New ordering and live-count regression
tests cover the shared helpers.

~~ Fix a Mac Catalyst finalizer crash pulled in by MAUI 10.0.41 ~~

After the UI smoke pass, the Mac Catalyst preview crashed with SIGSEGV
about 25 minutes into an otherwise idle review session. The finalizer
stack - MauiCALayerAutosizeToSuperLayerBehavior.Detach,
MauiCALayer.Dispose, NSObject.Finalize, GC.CallFinalize,
GC.GuardedFinalize - matches dotnet/maui#33800: MauiCALayer.Dispose(bool
disposing) called Detach(), an objc_msgSend on a native CALayer,
unconditionally, even when disposing is false during GC finalization
after UIKit may have already deallocated the native layer.

Bump only the gallery app's MauiVersion to 10.0.51; shipping SkiaSharp
dependencies and native sources are unchanged. dotnet/maui#33818 guards
the same cleanup behind "if (disposing)". A standalone IL check walked
each Dispose(bool) method for a branch on the disposing argument before
any native call opcode: the unconditional call was still present in
MauiCALayer, StaticCALayer, and StaticCAShapeLayer in the resolved
10.0.41 assembly, and guarded in all three in 10.0.51, confirmed
against both the NuGet package and the assembly inside the built app.
The patched process then ran 32 consecutive DevFlow status checks over
1860.2 seconds (31 minutes, 2026-10-02 04:23-04:54 UTC) with no crash,
exceeding the original ~25-minute failure interval. mono/SkiaSharp#3178
was compared and ruled out: a different Metal GRContext/command-queue
stack, with no fix for that issue claimed here.

5249.title: Add native GTK4 GPU rendering and pixel scaling
5249.body:
Add native GTK4 GPU rendering and pixel scaling (#5249)

Context: https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/signal.GLArea.render.html
Context: https://github.com/GNOME/gtk/blob/4.20.3/gtk/gtkglarea.c

Give GTK4 applications a GL-backed Skia canvas and an explicit
physical-versus-logical painting contract. Keep context ownership and
widget lifecycle with GTK, and demonstrate the views with native GTK
controls rather than introducing MAUI or Gallery dependencies. No Skia
C API or generated binding changes are needed.

~~ Let GTK own the GPU canvas lifecycle ~~

Add SKGLArea : Gtk.GLArea, named after its underlying native widget, with
PaintSurface and a protected virtual OnPaintSurface hook. Expose CanvasSize,
the view-owned GRContext, EnableRenderLoop and IgnorePixelScaling without
adding a separate context-change event or public resource-release API.
Callers use GTK's QueueRender for invalidation.

Create the Skia context lazily from the context supplied by GTK's render
signal. Recreate it when GTK supplies a different native context; abandon
displaced or unusable contexts rather than issuing cleanup against the
wrong GL context. Release surfaces before render targets and contexts on
unrealize/disposal. The render loop uses GTK tick callbacks, defaults off,
and removes its callback when disabled or unrealized. Skia factory results
are used directly, without a GTK-specific initialization-error translation
or CPU canvas fallback.

Add pre-context widget-default/render-loop smoke checks, reuse the existing
display initialization helper and copy native Skia assets into the test
host. The macOS GTK4 run passed 28 tests with four platform/display skips.
The new widget smoke test is Linux-targeted; actual macOS GUI rendering was
exercised separately on the application main thread.

~~ Resolve GL through GTK's current-context dispatcher ~~

An OS-specific GL import does not necessarily address GTK's chosen GL
implementation, particularly when Windows uses EGL/ANGLE rather than WGL.
The shared GlesInterop helper selects a library at compile time, so it
cannot follow that runtime context choice.

Add GtkGl using libepoxy, the dispatcher GTK's own GLArea implementation
uses. Leave GTK's default GL/GLES allow-list intact. Resolve both state
queries and Skia interface entry points through epoxy_<function> exports:
these exports are pointer variables, so dereference their addresses before
passing the callable pointers to Skia. Keep the library loaded for those
pointers' lifetime, use Winapi delegate conventions and return zero for a
missing procedure.

Load libepoxy.so.0 on Linux, libepoxy.0.dylib on macOS, or libepoxy-0.dll
with epoxy-0.dll as the Windows alternative. Report a missing dispatcher
with the required library names. GTK installations normally supply this
native dependency; manually bundled runtimes must include it. Add an
internal-access test for dispatch exports and the missing-symbol contract,
not a claim that symbol lookup alone proves GPU rendering.

~~ Describe GTK's bound framebuffer rather than assume its state ~~

GTK binds its buffers before emitting render and can change GL state and
attachments between paints. Reset Skia's cached GL state, query the bound
framebuffer and sample count, and rebuild the render target when dimensions,
framebuffer identity, sample count or stencil size change. Use RGBA8 and a
bottom-left origin, and clamp samples to Skia's supported surface count.

Read the stencil attachment's object type before querying
GL_FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_STENCIL_SIZE; an absent attachment contributes
zero bits. The legacy GL_STENCIL_BITS query is unsuitable for desktop core
profiles: the macOS probe reported zero through that path despite an
eight-bit attachment. Keep GL tokens in GtkGl with their exact header names
and values. Real macOS rendering verified the attachment size and red/blue
framebuffer orientation.

~~ Separate physical backing pixels from logical paint coordinates ~~

SKDrawingArea previously allocated its Cairo/Skia backing at GTK's logical
draw dimensions. Allocate at width/height multiplied by GetScaleFactor,
using checked arithmetic, and paint the backing into Cairo with an inverse
scale inside a saved/restored context.

Default CanvasSize and paint Info to physical pixels in the raster and
new GL views. Add IgnorePixelScaling to SKDrawingArea and provide it on
SKGLArea: enabling it scales the canvas and exposes logical Info while
RawInfo still describes physical backing pixels. This changes the raster
default on high-density displays; IgnorePixelScaling=true selects logical
coordinates without discarding backing resolution. GTK input coordinates
remain logical independently of that property.

The scale-two probe verified 1648x1536 physical backing and 824x768 logical
paint dimensions with unchanged RawInfo.

~~ Respect Cairo's borrowed pixel storage ~~

The raster SKSurface wraps Cairo-owned pixels, so dispose the Skia surface
before its Cairo.ImageSurface owner, reversing the previous release order.
Keep Cairo's stride when wrapping the buffer and throw
InvalidOperationException if SKSurface.Create returns null.

Keep the Cairo snapshot flush before the RGBA red/blue swizzle, but mark the
pixels dirty after the modification rather than before it. Reset CanvasSize
when the drawing objects are released.

~~ Keep drawing colors independent of GTK theme-name inference ~~

Remove DrawingPage.IsDarkMode and CanvasBackground, which chose drawing
colors from GtkApplicationPreferDarkTheme or a "dark" theme-name substring.
Use a fixed white canvas, black initial brush and standard six-color palette
instead of maintaining paired light/dark colors. GTK retains responsibility
for native chrome styling; the sample does not synchronize or override OS
appearance. This is a deliberate fixed drawing palette, not system-theme
support.

~~ Demonstrate GPU rendering with native sample controls ~~

Add the GPU page, its copied UI Builder layout and SamplePage.Gpu navigation.
Compile the SkSL metaball shader once, update time/resolution/pointer
uniforms per frame, and normalize pointer positions using logical widget
dimensions. Start/stop rendering on map/unmap; dispose the shader builder
and paint, and detach controllers and callbacks on disposal.

Use a native GTK box/label for the pointer-transparent FPS pill. White text
keeps it readable over the dark shader; update the label on a frame-clock
callback rather than while the GL paint/snapshot is being rendered. The
real sample probe rendered 203 frames with 189 distinct sampled center
colors, establishing animation rather than merely successful construction.

Group native drawing swatches and brush controls, show a blue selection
ring, improve Clear-button contrast and reflow the toolbox below 600 logical
pixels of available page width, excluding the sidebar. Consume brush-size
scroll events after adjusting the slider so they do not propagate as
unhandled input.

Align the README with the Basic samples, correct its default-SKFont and
.NET 10 requirements, and document GTK setup, including Homebrew's native
library search path. Capture CPU, GPU and Drawing at 1024x768 through GTK's
scene graph so screenshots include native controls, not just a GPU surface.

Runtime proof is macOS arm64 with GTK 4.20.3. Windows x64 was cross-built,
not executed; Linux and Windows GTK/GL runtime behavior remains unverified.
The unfiltered console suite was not green: ganesh-gl/DiagonalLines had
1,832 outlier pixels against 1,310 allowed, and the final run also failed
SKManagedStreamTest.StreamIsCollectedEvenWhenNotProperlyDisposed.
Stream-lifetime failures varied across runs. No core tests, golden images
or their skip policies are changed by this PR.

~~ Release freehand drawing resources at their owning boundaries ~~

SKPathBuilder.Detach returns a path and resets the builder; it does not
delete the builder's native handle. Dispose the completed builder after
detaching its stroke instead of dropping the managed reference. Cancel and
dispose an unfinished builder when the page unmaps, and clear stale hover
state.

On DrawingPage disposal, stop the layout tick, detach map/unmap and paint
handlers, and dispose retained stroke paths and swatch CSS providers. Keep
stroke ownership with the page while preserving completed strokes across
ordinary palette, brush-size and visibility changes.

5277.title: Provision Microsoft OpenJDK 21 for Android builds
5277.body:
Provision Microsoft OpenJDK 21 for Android builds (#5277)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/5271
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5266
Context: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/android/getting-started/installation/dependencies

Select the recommended Android JDK, keep its download and extracted-home
versions consistent, and validate the selected tools before exposing them
to subsequent build steps. Carry forward the JDK upgrade from #5266
without its SDK, workload, Android API, or Apple provisioning changes.

~~ Select JDK 21 for the existing Android provisioning path ~~

The installer defaulted to Microsoft OpenJDK 17.0.8.1 and looked
specifically for JAVA_HOME_17_X64. Microsoft recommends OpenJDK 21 for
.NET for Android. Default to 21.0.10+7 and derive the agent reuse variable
from the requested major, so JAVA_HOME_21_X64 supplies the existing JDK.

Keep provisioning under the existing installAndroidSdk guard and document
JAVA_HOME and PATH setup for local Android builds. This changes Android
Java provisioning, not browser-WASM dependencies.

A real Windows build of SkiaSharp.Tests.Devices for net10.0-android passed
with SDK 10.0.401, Android workload 36.1.43, and Microsoft JDK 21.0.10.
The initial build produced signed and unsigned APKs; the single-version
implementation passed the Android build again. Device execution was not
validated.

~~ Keep download and archive-home identity in one version ~~

The separate Version and FolderVersion parameters required callers to
coordinate a release number with its build-qualified archive directory.
Replace FolderVersion with a full Version such as 21.0.10+7, and add the
shared OPENJDK_VERSION pin to the existing bootstrapper invocation.

Microsoft's download URLs use the portion before '+', while the archive
home uses jdk-<full-version>, with Contents/Home appended on macOS.
Require the numeric release+build form before installation starts.
Overrides now use forms such as -Version '17.0.8.1+1'.

A real Windows download through the derived 21.0.10 URL extracted into
jdk-21.0.10+7 and ran Java and javac successfully. A real JDK 17 override
also passed. This follows the Microsoft archive layout, not a universal
directory convention across OpenJDK vendors.

~~ Reject invalid selected installations before exporting them ~~

An existing bin directory did not establish that the reused home contained
a usable JDK or the requested Java major. Check the selected home's java
and javac executables directly: require each file, a successful -version
exit, and output identifying the requested major before exporting
JAVA_HOME or updating PATH.

Preserve requested-major reuse rather than demanding an exact patch/build
match. A nonempty agent home is authoritative: an invalid home fails
instead of silently switching to a download. Also check tar's exit code
explicitly; PowerShell's Stop preference alone does not propagate that
native-command failure.

Advertising a real JDK 17 home as JAVA_HOME_21_X64 failed before environment
export. Windows cold installation and reuse passed; macOS/Linux execution
and the tar failure path were not exercised.

~~ Make command lookup agree with JAVA_HOME ~~

The previous PATH substring check left the selected bin directory in its
existing position when already present. An older Java earlier on PATH
could therefore remain the executable used by command-line consumers.

Prepend the validated bin directory in the current process and emit
Azure's task.prependpath command for subsequent tasks. Export the actual
selected home rather than inferring a Windows installer directory from
the archive name. Real Windows reuse resolved java and javac under
C:\Program Files\Microsoft\jdk-21.0.10.7-hotspot\bin.

The unfiltered net10.0 console solution still reported three failures:
SKColorSpaceTest.ColorSpaceIsNotDisposedPrematurely expected reference
count 4 but observed 3, and two GPU ImageCanClearBackground cases expected
#ffe98404 but observed #ffe88404. Those tests do not consume Java; their
failures are not Android build evidence. Assertions, skips, and tolerances
remain unchanged, and the PR records the commands and results.

5279.title: Use native generator line endings and adapt cross-OS comparisons
5279.body:
Use native generator line endings and adapt cross-OS comparisons (#5279)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/37349308898

Generate bindings with the host's native line endings while distinguishing
local byte-exact checks from cross-platform content comparisons. Keep Git's
text normalization responsible for the committed representation rather than
forcing Windows generation to use Unix line endings.

~~ Match native checkout line endings ~~

CreateOutputWriter explicitly set StreamWriter.NewLine to LF. With
core.autocrlf=true, Windows checked out the committed generated sources as
CRLF, but regeneration wrote LF. Git normalized this difference away, while
the Skia review's filesystem byte comparison reported mismatches.

Remove the explicit newline override and use StreamWriter's
Environment.NewLine default: CRLF on Windows and LF on Linux/macOS. This
covers the shared writer used for generated declarations and native aliases.

Regenerating the five maintained binding projects on Windows produced 355
CRLF files with no generated-file Git diff or new binding files. Their
output copies matched byte-for-byte. Custom Git settings can still select
endings different from the OS default; generation does not inspect or
override that checkout policy.

~~ Compare cross-platform content without hiding other differences ~~

The determinism workflow uploads Linux, macOS and Windows output, then
compares the downloaded trees on Linux. Matching each runner's checkout
does not make those artifacts byte-identical: Windows now contributes CRLF
while Linux and macOS contribute LF. The referenced run completed generation
on all three platforms but failed the cross-platform comparison.

Use diff --strip-trailing-cr for that recursive comparison and
git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol for its failure reports. Rename the step and
success message so they no longer promise byte-for-byte equality. Keep the
checked-in freshness check and Skia review comparator byte-exact; those
check different contracts and do not need cross-OS newline equivalence.

Executing the updated comparison block against the failed run's artifacts
passed both platform comparisons. Seven temporary regression cases accepted
CRLF-only differences while rejecting code, documentation, trailing-space,
missing-final-newline, missing-file and added-file differences. Content
failures still produced nonempty diagnostic diffs.

5275.title: Test .NET 10 and 11 package consumers in each desktop job
5275.body:
Test .NET 10 and 11 package consumers in each desktop job (#5275)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/5271
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1623663

Keep SDK provisioning in CI and consumer framework coverage in the tests.
Extend the packaged-asset baseline to .NET 11 without adding a separate CI
job for each target framework or changing shipped package dependencies.

~~ Make target frameworks explicit rather than infer them from the SDK ~~

The existing 22 console-consumer cases hardcode net10.0. Running those
cases with a newer SDK would still prove only net10.0 package consumption:
an SDK version and a project's target framework are independent choices.

Run the existing default-package and RID scenarios with explicit net10.0
and net11.0 theory inputs for both SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp, producing
44 single-target cases. Include the framework in each generated project's
name and assert its restored framework set and runtimeconfig TFM, rather
than accepting a successful compiler exit as proof of framework coverage.

Retain the original native path-set and SHA-256 comparisons against real
package archives, exact package versions, artifact-only family sourcing,
and private restore cache. These tests inspect restore/build/publish asset
layout; they do not execute foreign-RID applications or native graphics.

~~ Provision the preview SDK without introducing a second version policy ~~

The repository's stable SDK selection cannot build net11.0 consumers.
Opt the existing Windows, macOS and Linux MSBuild package-test jobs into
installPreviewSdk, reusing the bootstrapper's SDK installation and job-local
global.json selection. Keep the stable runtime alongside the preview SDK
so the standalone test runner can remain net10.0.

Use the shared DOTNET_VERSION and DOTNET_VERSION_PREVIEW settings instead
of duplicating SDK release pins in stage YAML or documentation. Keep the
existing preview-6 SDK/workload pairing and browser job unchanged; desktop
package tests continue to install no workloads or native build tools.
Generated consumers retain the existing exact selected-SDK pin with
roll-forward disabled, independently of their explicit target frameworks.
Document the preview SDK selection required for local consumer-test runs.

~~ Exercise genuine multi-target builds without output collisions ~~

Two single-target projects do not establish that one console project with
TargetFrameworks=net10.0;net11.0 builds and publishes correctly. Add four
cases covering build and publish for each package family, with explicit
Linux native assets alongside the default Windows and macOS assets.

Build the outer multi-target project without --framework or a shared -o,
then inspect both normal per-framework output trees. Publish each framework
separately into its own directory and recheck both trees after publishing
to detect cross-framework overwrites. Verify native paths and hashes,
restored framework sets and each output's runtime TFM.

Give each publish invocation separate command, stdout/stderr and binlog
artifacts. Preserve per-framework assets, dependency and runtimeconfig
metadata before deleting successful build outputs; retain failed outputs
and the existing five-minute process timeout. This makes failures in either
framework diagnosable without the second publish replacing the first log.

Public Complete run 1623663 passed this 48-case suite on Windows x64,
macOS ARM64 and Linux x64, with zero failures or skips. Downloaded TRX and
consumer artifacts verified 144 actual projects and 156 framework outputs.
All three jobs selected the configured preview SDK and consumed that run's
original packages. The eight required packages' nuspec IDs and versions
were verified, and their repository commits matched the PR head.
Whole-package SHA-512 and native SHA-256 manifests were retained.
This is proof of the desktop MSBuild stage, not broader workload coverage.

Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1618579

Linux dependencies or RID filtering. Exercise generated PackageReference

    application.
  * RuntimeIdentifiers=linux-x64;linux-arm64 supplies restore targets, not
    an output allow-list: RID-less build/publish still retain those
    packages' Windows and macOS assets as well as Linux assets.
  * Publishing with -r linux-x64 selects flattened x64 assets and overrides
    the project's singular ARM64 RID.

NativeAssetOutputTests compares native library path sets and SHA-256 hashes
with entries in the real package archives, and requires the managed family
assembly in output. Derive expectations from package contents rather than
historical binary counts or sizes. These are output-selection tests, not
native-load, rendering, legacy ShouldIncludeNative, or mobile/WASM tests;
foreign-RID applications are built but not executed.

~~ Keep consumer restores independent of source builds and stale caches ~~

Use a standalone .NET 10 xUnit v3/Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner.
Local Directory.Build.props/targets barriers prevent the runner and its
generated consumers from inheriting the repository's source-build imports.
Keep project definitions and assertions in NativeAssetOutputTests, with
Utils/DotNet handling project creation and actual build/publish commands.

Read versions from nuspec metadata, reject missing or ambiguous matching
archives, exclude symbol packages, and use exact PackageReference versions.
Map SkiaSharp* and HarfBuzzSharp* exclusively to the supplied artifact
directory; unrelated dependencies remain restorable from dotnet-public.
Consumer restores share one fresh private cache per test-class execution,
with separate project/intermediate/output directories for each case.
This avoids reusing same-version packages from the user's global cache
without repeatedly restoring into a new cache for every matrix row.

Capture the runner's SDK version and dotnet host, and disable SDK
roll-forward for consumers. Drain stdout/stderr concurrently, retain both
streams and binlogs, and terminate the command's process tree after a
five-minute timeout. Preserve failed outputs; after successful assertions,
retain restore/dependency metadata and discard build outputs. Dispose the
private cache without clearing user caches. An empty-artifact validation
failed explicitly in the four default-package cases rather than falling
back to published packages.

~~ Report package failures without delaying existing source tests ~~

Add tests-msbuild as an independent Cake target and an MSBuild package
tests stage with Windows, macOS, and Linux jobs. Include the stage in
complete and test pipelines, not the build-only pipeline.

Combined CI depends on package and consumes its current-run nuget artifact.
Downstream Tests depends on prepare and consumes the exact SkiaSharp
pipeline-resource build. Reuse the existing build-ID artifact convention,
placing packages in output/nugets. The stage runs alongside Samples;
existing source/unit/device test prerequisites remain unchanged.

Disable submodule checkout and workload/mobile/native tool provisioning
for these jobs. Run dotnet cake --target=tests-msbuild without automatic
test retries, publish TRX even on failure, and fail on failed tests or
missing results. Publish command logs, binlogs, generated projects,
dependency metadata, and failed outputs from output/logs. Document the
artifact prerequisite and direct dotnet test invocation in the build guide.
The existing Integration and release-testing entry points remain intact.

passed 22/22 package tests on each of Windows, macOS, and Linux. The final

source console run retained an existing ganesh-gl/DiagonalLines mismatch:
1,832 pixels exceeded tolerance against 1,310 allowed. That failure was
reproduced in a focused run; no golden files, tolerances, or skips changed.

5208.title: Integrate the m155 core fork cleanup on current main
5208.body:
Integrate the m155 core fork cleanup on current main (#5208)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/385
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/bde355dbafafcd485b0df033cc67e7ae6fd29c5c...149e3e4fc360b887a1cb70432c4ddeda36bf2c5b

metadata differences from upstream chrome/m155 while preserving functional
fork behavior and compatibility required by supported toolchains.

The parent diff changes only externals/skia and its matching mono/skia
commitHash in cgmanifest.json. Windows and Tizen modernization are already
in the main baseline; this change does not reintroduce their build edits,
advance the milestone, or modify managed APIs and generated declarations.

~~ Restore upstream constructs without dropping supported WASM paths ~~

The native cleanup restores typed arrays, pointer accessors, defaulted
C++20 comparisons, optional::emplace and standard concept constraints that
had been rewritten for older compilers. It also restores direct
emscripten/version.h includes instead of the Emscripten 2.x fallback.

SkPDFTag uses reverse iterators instead of std::views::reverse, and
SkSVGDevice uses std::find_if instead of the ranges projection lookup.
Restoring those upstream expressions would break that build configuration.
SkTextBlob::allocRunRSXform bounds forwarding remains intact, independently
of the restored scalar-count table.

The upstream audit checked the dropped patches against chrome/m155
6cc992aeb38230d744923902da6ea9d622e90063. Its 45 removed upstream-relative
patches match the reference blobs, or their paths are absent in both trees.
The four adapted patches preserve their functional/build/WASM purposes.
The review artifacts are output/ai/repos/mono-skia/ai-review/385.json and
the corresponding HTML report.

A fresh Cake Windows x64 MSVC source build passed. SkiaSharp and
HarfBuzzSharp linked libcmt, libcpmt and libvcruntime from the selected
MSVC 14.44.35207 Spectre x64 libraries and retained CFG/security-cookie
instrumentation. Independent generation/compare CI passed. The local
byte-exact generator check remained FAIL, but its 355 differing files
contained CRLF/LF differences rather than substantive binding changes.

violation did not reproduce in isolation or the full rerun. Assertions,

source entry. This helper supplied signed multiplication-with-overflow
support on 32-bit targets whose compiler runtime lacked __mulodi4.

The shared native recipe already sets skia_use_dng_sdk=false and
skia_use_piex=false, so the DNG consumer is not compiled. Removal does not
prove that every 32-bit runtime supplies the symbol. Re-enabling DNG or
adding another overflow caller requires appropriate compiler-runtime

5238.title: Align Windows v143 builds and verify Spectre provenance
5238.body:
Align Windows v143 builds and verify Spectre provenance (#5238)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5207
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5208
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5231
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1618997

Select a coherent installed v143 toolset and matching Spectre CRT for the
Windows native builds, propagate security flags through ANGLE's GN defaults,
and keep generated WinUI projection paths short. This branch retains main's
Skia pin bde355dbafafcd485b0df033cc67e7ae6fd29c5c; the separate core
cleanup in #5231 is not required for this Windows build change.

~~ Select one installed v143 compiler and CRT ~~

The base requested 14.2 for Skia GN and vcvars, targeted v142 for HarfBuzz,
and chose the first installed Spectre library directory independently of
both. This could mix toolset versions or select an incomplete installation.
Read the selected VS installation's general default when it is v143
(14.30-14.49), otherwise use its v143-specific default. Supply the full
version to Skia's win_toolchain_version, vcvars, and MSBuild; Skia's
win_vcvars_version takes the 14.3/14.4 prefix instead. Look for Spectre
libraries under that exact compiler version and fail if the target
architecture's directory is absent. The old --vcToolsetVersion argument is
no longer used; --vsinstall or VS_INSTALL selects the installation.

The local VS 2022 general default was complete at 14.44.35207, whereas its
v143-specific default pointed to an incomplete 14.42. WinUI and HarfBuzz
receive the selected VCToolsVersion through the existing MSBuild properties;
WinUI also aligns CsWinRT metadata with an explicitly selected Windows SDK.
The build guide now describes the necessary v143/Spectre and WinUI C++
components and selection options, not GN or PDB implementation details.
Fresh x64 Windows MSVC, Clang, and NanoServer source builds passed.

~~ Verify native Spectre CRT provenance, not full mitigation ~~

Set MSBuild SpectreMitigation=Spectre for HarfBuzz and native WinUI. Skia's
existing compiler and linker /guard:cf remain, with its Spectre /LIBPATH
pointed at the selected compiler version. CheckWindowsDependencies now
rejects checked native DLLs whose adjacent PDB lacks an objr_spectre or
objd_spectre runtime build marker. The managed WinUI projection explicitly
opts out: it has no native CRT to identify. A marker establishes CRT
provenance, not whole-program /Qspectre instrumentation; this change does
not add GN /Qspectre. The x64 PDBs identified the selected Spectre CRT,
MSBuild compiler logs showed /GS /guard:cf /Qspectre, and the audited PE
images had CFG function tables and nonzero security cookies.

~~ Propagate ANGLE hardening through Chromium GN defaults ~~

The base supplied extra_cflags and extra_ldflags as ANGLE GN arguments,
which did not reach all third-party compilation. Copy a repository-owned
skiasharp GN config into ANGLE and attach it to BUILDCONFIG.gn's
default_compiler_configs, rather than an ANGLE-only config. This gives
eligible compiler commands /guard:cf and /GS and linker commands /guard:cf
plus the matching Spectre /LIBPATH. Pass the chosen VS installation and
VCToolsVersion to GN's process environment and restore the prior depot-tools
toolchain setting afterwards. The x64 Ninja command audit checked ANGLE and
third-party ASTC/zlib/volk commands; fresh regular libEGL and WinAppSDK
libGLESv2 source builds passed. Cake.FileHelpers handles ANGLE's text-file
updates, while GN reads the versioned config and tracks its changes.

~~ Avoid VS 2022 projection path-length failures ~~

Deep project-local bin/obj paths risked exceeding VS 2022 MSBuild's path
limits for generated WinUI projection filenames. Write projection working
outputs under repository-root artifacts/bin and artifacts/obj, exclude the
old local bin/obj paths from project items, and stage the final DLL/PDB into
output/native/winui/any. Native WinUI DLL/PDB/WinMD staging remains
architecture-specific. The fresh x64 WinUI source build produced both the
native component and managed projection.

Azure run 1618997 tested the code at 23d2580 before the documentation-only
follow-up. Its Native Windows, managed, packaging, and Tests stages passed,
including Windows .NET Core and Framework jobs. The unfiltered local console
suite had two GPU ImageCanClearBackground pixel mismatches that CI did not
reproduce. The aggregate run failed before Linux sample compilation when
Android CLI provisioning returned HTTP 404; the separate Windows benchmark
runner selected VS 2026 without matching v143 Spectre libraries. Neither
failure is changed or hidden by this Windows-only PR.

5235.title: Require Tizen 10 GCC 14.2 builds and packaging
5235.body:
Require Tizen 10 GCC 14.2 builds and packaging (#5235)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/387
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5222
Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/383
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/0abb58b1b29cc8dd28aa604709af324e0d2d1682...bde355dbafafcd485b0df033cc67e7ae6fd29c5c

Make Tizen 10 and GCC 14.2 the direct x64/arm64 build minimum on the
current m155 main baseline, and align Tizen native packages with that
platform floor. Carry the Tizen work reviewed in #5222 and mono/skia#383
without their separate core compiler cleanup. This does not introduce
m156 sources, a Windows toolset change, or a new managed or C API.

~~ Select the Tizen 10 compiler directly ~~

At the base, Cake built against Tizen 8 rootstraps with the LLVM compiler
selection. Native GN defaulted to a GCC 9.2 tool directory but invoked
LLVM 10 Clang, retaining Clang-specific --target and c++2a flags and
older x64 ISA spellings. Cake now selects the Tizen 10 64-bit rootstraps,
uses `build-native -c gcc` for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp, and passes
10.0/14.2 versions matching the native GN defaults.

GN resolves the installed target-prefixed GCC drivers, retains the Tizen
sysroot and binutils paths, uses C++20 and x86-64-v3/v4 flags, and rejects
Tizen CPUs other than x64 and arm64. The former GCC opt-in, Clang 10 and
32-bit selection paths are not fallbacks. Keep `-fno-rtti` in C++ options
rather than passing it to the GCC C compiler. Fresh-image source builds
produced Tizen x64 and arm64 SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp libraries.

~~ Provision the SDK version the build requires ~~

The former container installed Tizen 8 CLI packages and depended on
LLVM 10 and the older GCC tool directory. Its installation no longer
matched the required compiler or rootstraps. Install the official
Tizen 10 native CLI package and NativeToolchain-Gcc-14.2 instead; check
for both 64-bit rootstraps and both GCC cross-compiler executables while
building the image. The LLVM 10 host compatibility package is no longer
needed. The fresh SDK image built, and the source builds used that image.

~~ Preserve Clang annotations under GCC warnings-as-errors ~~

Skia template reset methods used [[clang::reinitializes]] directly.
GCC 14.2 diagnoses that Clang-only annotation under the existing
warning-as-error policy. SK_REINITIALIZES now uses
__has_cpp_attribute(clang::reinitializes): supporting Clang compilers
retain the annotation, while GCC omits it without suppressing warnings.
The Tizen source builds passed with this guard.

~~ Keep paint assignment warning-clean ~~

SkCompatPaint::reset already assigns a temporary, but SkCompatPaint
declared a copy constructor without an explicit copy-assignment
operator. GCC warns about the implicit assignment, failing this build
under -Werror. Explicitly default that operator in the declaration and
definition. This preserves the assignment behavior and changes no
exported C API; both Tizen architectures compiled successfully.

~~ Align Tizen package and app floors ~~

The base NativeAssets projects included previous, current, and minimum
Tizen TFMs, while shared properties advertised an older platform
minimum. Both Tizen NativeAssets projects now target
net10.0-tizen10.0; the shared Tizen minimum properties are 10.0, without
changing the non-Tizen .NET minimum. The sample moves from
net6.0-tizen8.0 to net10.0-tizen10.0 and declares manifest API 10.
The device-test project raises SupportedOSPlatformVersion to 10, but
its separate Tizen manifest still declares API 8. Tizen 8/9 are not
supported by these new native builds and packages; that test-manifest
mismatch and Tizen 10 device/package loading remain unvalidated.

The macOS ARM64 native source build and managed build passed. The
unfiltered net10 macOS console suite did not: Ganesh GL DiagonalLines
differed at 1,832 of 65,536 pixels against 1,310 allowed, also
reproduced with the original main native pin. A managed-stream GC test
failed in an earlier run but passed its focused and final full reruns;
its intermittent failure remains unresolved. This is not a passing
console-suite or Tizen runtime result.

~~ Pin the reviewed native tree, not its unmerged head ~~

Pin externals/skia and cgmanifest.json from
0abb58b1b29cc8dd28aa604709af324e0d2d1682 to the squash-merged
mono/skia#387 commit bde355dbafafcd485b0df033cc67e7ae6fd29c5c.
That single-parent commit does not contain the reviewed head
a59697b050f0b43eabc3067958a489728d4c662e in its ancestry, but
both have the exact tree b2a3f4af50415e5d9280e29e292c429e35a200b1.
The final parent repin changes the gitlink and manifest, not the native
source that was built. The native fork-patch audit against upstream m155
passed, with the obsolete Tizen Clang 10 ISA hunk deliberately removed
and unrelated fork changes retained. The compare link records the
complete native pointer range.

5086.title: Restore Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery
5086.body:
Restore Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery (#5086)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4303
Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/364
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/6a3f259016481f7b5ce70bb7f511fd79c3005458...0abb58b1b29cc8dd28aa604709af324e0d2d1682

Restore directory-backed default font discovery for
SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux.NoDependencies without introducing a
fontconfig dependency. Pin externals/skia and cgmanifest.json to the
native merge commit 0abb58b1b29cc8dd28aa604709af324e0d2d1682, preserving
the current m155 baseline.

After the migration away from SkFontMgr::Factory(), the affected
no-fontconfig Linux builds fell through sk_fontmgr_create_default's
selection chain to SkFontMgr_New_Custom_Empty(). That manager reports
one nameless family and supplies empty typefaces whose OpenStream()
returns null. Family-based font resolution therefore failed despite
installed fonts, and SKShaper construction threw ArgumentNullException
for the asset parameter. Explicitly loading a font file still worked.

The native fix selects
SkFontMgr_New_Custom_Directory(SK_FONT_FILE_PREFIX) when
SK_FONTMGR_FREETYPE_DIRECTORY_AVAILABLE is defined. The prefix defaults
to /usr/share/fonts/ while respecting a build-supplied override, matching
the former SkFontMgr_custom_directory_factory.cpp behavior. Existing
platform-specific and fontconfig branches retain precedence. A scan that
discovers no fonts retains the loader's existing empty-family fallback.

The GN dependency is necessary, not just a linking adjustment:
src/c/sk_typeface.cpp compiles in :core, whereas the directory manager
previously belonged to :skia. Add :fontmgr_custom_directory to :core for
Linux/Tizen when fontconfig is disabled and the directory manager is
enabled. This supplies the availability define to the C API compilation;
the source change alone would leave the new branch inactive.

The native merge includes newer baseline history, so its complete tree
is not identical to the original reviewed head. Against the native
revision already pinned by main, its delta is the two-file font-manager
fix, with the same stable patch ID as the reviewed change. The parent
diff changes the gitlink and manifest reference without changing managed
APIs or generated bindings.

The contributor's source-built Linux NoDependencies x64 A/B reproduction,
with DejaVu and Ubuntu fonts installed, changed FontFamilyCount from one
to seven. DejaVu Sans lookup changed from an empty typeface with a null
stream to the named font with a 759720-byte stream; unavailable Arial
fell back to DejaVu Serif. Compiler-command inspection confirmed that
the GN dependency supplied the directory-manager define. The original
reproduction did not exercise Tizen, and no automated regression test
was added.

5185.title: [release] Enable chat-driven publication and improve release audits
5185.body:
[release] Enable chat-driven publication and improve release audits (#5185)

Context: https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/38967

Let maintainers prepare, publish, and finish a SkiaSharp release from chat
without bypassing the protected publication gate. Make the release audit
distinguish usable BAR evidence from failed reruns and show draft Skia sync
work that still needs review.

~~ Protected package publication ~~

Previously, release guidance stopped at a team-owned publication procedure;
the release-publish skill could not queue packages. On an explicit request,
it now verifies the exact SkiaSharp release-branch commit, succeeded Build
and resource-triggered Tests runs, matching BAR, and any existing publication
run before queuing the official MAUI release pipeline. It requires the
pipeline default and internal mirror to use merged MAUI main, then checks the
resolved MAUI source SHA and the separate SkiaSharp BAR commit after dispatch.

The pipeline prepares a NuGetReleaseAudit and waits at ManualValidation
before its protected NuGet job. Preparation is not approval: a human checks
the BAR, package identities, ownership, and quota. After approval, verify
the exact shipping packages on NuGet.org; a partial publish must not trigger
an automatic retry or release finalization.

~~ Release preparation handoff ~~

Make release-branch guidance executable from chat: dispatch Release - Prepare
on main with push=false, inspect its plan, and require confirmation before
repeating the same inputs with push=true. Verify the resulting paired release
branches rather than treating a successful dispatch as a completed cut.
Keep the local preparation script as a fallback, not a route around workflow
verification or a trigger for package publication.

~~ Public release finalization ~~

After the complete package set is public, use Release - Finish on main with
push=false to review the exact tag, source commit, and follow-up plan. Require
a separate confirmation before push=true. Local Finish remains a fallback;
it cannot replace the MAUI pipeline's NuGet approval or justify finalizing a
failed or partial publication.

~~ Exact-tip package build selection ~~

The audit previously chose the newest result from a 20-build lookup. A newer
failed or canceled rerun could therefore hide a succeeded build and BAR for
the same release-branch commit; an older eligible run could also fall beyond
that limit. Page the internal build history, prefer the newest fully
succeeded exact-tip build with one BAR, and report newer unsuccessful
attempts without letting them displace it.

If no succeeded BAR exists, expose a partially succeeded build with a BAR
for review, not publication. A partial build without usable BAR evidence
still requires a fix or rerun. Publishing-script regressions cover those
selection, pagination, and readiness boundaries.

~~ Draft Skia sync review visibility ~~

An upstream comparison can appear current against an unmerged sync branch
while its draft PR still needs review. Add a review-sync action for draft
incoming PRs without blocking an otherwise valid release cut, and require
the audit summary to link the native mono/skia PR alongside its SkiaSharp
companion. This separates pending PR review from both an upstream change
and a release-cut blocker.
